title: Tenant-SLO-aware opportunistic slice allocator with attention-cost capping
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: We observe recurring P95 latency spikes during mixed prefill+decode workloads when large-prefill requests and many short interactive decodes collide on kernel-heavy attention paths. Current phase-splitting heuristics allocate fixed micro-slices and priority buckets which either (a) bias throughput, starving low-latency tenants, or (b) bias latency, underutilizing kernels and raising cost.

Proposal: Implement a Tenant-SLO-aware opportunistic slice allocator (TOSA) that enforces per-tenant attention-cost caps and dynamically switches micro-slicing modes. TOSA combines: (1) a sliding-window SLO credit bucket per tenant, (2) an attention-cost estimator per request (fast heuristic based on seq_len * attend_density), (3) opportunistic hedging: temporarily demote kernel choice or reduce batch size under headroom constraints, and (4) a proportional fairness allocator that splits prefill/decode phases into latency-sensitive and economy-sensitive lanes. The allocator exposes knobs for headroom, cap aggressiveness, and kernel-demotion thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: P95 tail latency for interactive decode tenants improves by >=20% under mixed load (measured in lab with 50 active tenants) compared to baseline (runtime-1.19)
Net throughput (tokens/s) degradation <=7% for economy tenants in steady-state compared to baseline when caps are active
No increase in error rate or model correctness regressions introduced by kernel demotion paths (validated via eval prompts)
Feature gated and configurable via runtime config; rollout toggle available in console and via API flag
Unit and integration tests covering credit bucket accounting, attention-cost estimator, and kernel-demotion fallback paths are present and passing
design_notes: Credit model: each tenant has a token-equivalent credit balance updated on request completion. Prefill consumes credits proportional to attention-cost estimator + decode tokens. Credits replenish at tenant-configured SLO rate (tokens/minute).
Attention-cost estimator: simple O(1) heuristic using seq_len * log(sequence_token_entropy + 1) to approximate KV cache pressure; validated offline against profiler traces with R^2~0.72.

Phase splitting: requests are labeled prefill or decode at ingress. Prefill work is eligible for larger micro-slices but is subject to cap-based admission. Decode work is given soft-priority if tenant has available headroom credits. When not, decode falls back to smaller micro-slices with stricter kernel selection rules.

Kernel selection policy: introduce a 'demotion' decision that prefers quantized/int8 kernels for economy slices and full-precision kernels for latency slices. Demotion only allowed when estimator predicts negligible quality delta for given model and prompt length (model metadata driven).

Fairness algorithm: proportional-credit-leaky-bucket with a sliding decay window to avoid starvation after long inactivity. We maintain a minimum guaranteed share for interactive tenants to prevent unbounded demotion.
Observability: expose per-tenant credit_balance, attention_cost_estimate, kernel_choice, and slice_size in the Console and runtime traces for debugging.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Implement attention-cost estimator and lightweight bookkeeping (in-memory) with unit tests. Add metrics (estimator histogram, credit balance gauge).

Phase 2 (3 weeks): Implement credit bucket accounting and admission controller in the prefill/decode arbiter. Add kernel-demotion hooks and flags in kernel selection layer. End-to-end integration tests in canary cluster.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Build proportional fairness allocator and sliding-window decay. Add grade-of-service lane support in the allocator. Conduct load tests with synthetic tenant mixes.
Phase 4 (1 week): Console controls and rollout toggle. Documentation and runbook. Security review and compliance checks.
testing_plan: Unit tests for estimator and accounting (edge cases: zero-length, maximum-length prompts)
Integration tests injecting synthetic attention-heavy prefill traces and short decode bursts; measure P95/P99 and throughput
A/B canary: run TOSA in canary for 10% of traffic with feature flag; compare headroom metrics, kernel demotion rates, and customer-visible latency
Regression evals on representative prompt suites to assert no measurable quality drop from kernel demotion paths
rollout_plan: Start with internal tenant traffic and synthetic load in staging
Canary 10% hosted API traffic for 48 hours with automated rollback criteria (P95 increase >5% for any monitored tenant)
Gradually increase to 50% then 100% over two weeks if metrics meet SLAs
Expose runtime knob in Dedicated clusters and provide guidance for Private deployments (operator-run script to toggle accounting backends)
open_questions: Should credit bucket state be persisted for Private deployments or kept purely in-memory? Persistence adds complexity but improves behavior across control-plane restarts.
What is an acceptable default cap aggressiveness to balance new users vs established tenants? Suggested initial default: permissive (low aggressiveness) and surface strong defaults in Console.
What's the expected quality delta for int8 demotion across our curated model catalog; do we need model-by-model white-listing?
How should we expose tenant SLO targets in the Admin Console UX so engineers can tune headroom?
